stem.en: A steel bicycle in Chennai rusts faster than the same bicycle in Jodhpur. Kabir says "Chennai has more oxygen". What is the better reason?

text.en: Chennai's air is humid and salty from the sea. Rust needs water with the oxygen, and salt makes it faster. Jodhpur's air is dry.

feedback.en: Air is a fifth oxygen everywhere. The difference is the water and the salt.

text.en: Jodhpur's sand scrubs the rust off.

feedback.en: Sand scratches, which if anything exposes fresh iron. The dry air simply gives rust nothing to work with.
Heat speeds most reactions a little, but Jodhpur is often hotter than Chennai. Dry heat rusts slowly.

explanation.en: Ask what the reaction needs, then ask which place supplies it. Rust needs oxygen, water and, ideally, salt. Only one city offers all three.
